_comment: STAGE-D per-batch coverage registry -- batch 'stim_io' (D23, Tier-2 frontend cluster)
(docs/twin_validation/wave2_6_unit_test_contract.md SS12.3/12.4; full-coverage program;
work-list docs/twin_validation/l3_release_package_unit_inventory.md D23).
Run via tests/harness/gate.py <this file> (L0+L1; calls tests/harness/coverage_audit.py) and
tests/harness/mutation.py <this file> (L2).
MODULE: frontend/stim_io.py -- the Stim adapters the simulator frontend uses to move between the
key-based CircuitIR and concrete stim.Circuit/DetectorErrorModel artifacts. It imports NEITHER
torch NOR quimb (numpy + a lazy `import stim` inside circuit_to_stim / load_stim_circuit), so
EVERY public unit is CPU-PURE and IN-SCOPE for full L0+L1+L2 -- out_of_scope is therefore {} (the
AST reconcile refuses any gpu_bound claim on a torch-less module -> expect ZERO out_of_scope).
SEVEN public units (AST reconcile _public_units_in_module: top-level public defs + every public
method of a top-level class). StimCounts is a plain frozen dataclass with NO methods (only field
annotations), so it contributes NO units; the seven units are the seven module-level functions:
* circuit_to_stim            -- CircuitIR -> stim.Circuit (QUBIT_COORDS loop + per-step dispatch).
* load_stim_circuit          -- stim.Circuit.from_file(str(path)).
* write_stim_circuit         -- Path(path).write_text(str(circuit)); return the Path.
* write_detector_error_model -- Path(path).write_text(str(dem)); return the Path.
* detector_error_model       -- circuit.detector_error_model(decompose_errors=...).
* counts                     -- StimCounts(num_detectors/observables/measurements/qubits).
* sample_detector_records    -- seeded detector sampler -> (det, obs) bool arrays sliced by count.
The private helpers _record_targets / _qubit_coords_from_metadata are NOT public units (leading `_`),
so the coverage audit does not score them -- but they ARE mutated by mutmut and are exercised
end-to-end through circuit_to_stim (every reachable branch of _qubit_coords_from_metadata is tripped
with the EXACT message; the _record_targets happy path is covered by circuit_to_stim's DETECTOR /
OBSERVABLE routes; its two DEFENSIVE raises are structurally unreachable via a valid CircuitIR --
see REACHABILITY below).
L2 DISCIPLINE (100% coverage != discrimination).
* circuit_to_stim: the emitted stim.Circuit is pinned OP-BY-OP against an INDEPENDENT hand-built
stim.Circuit (built from stim primitives, NOT from circuit_to_stim) exercising ALL FIVE step
kinds (GateOp H/CX, Tick, MeasureOp, DetectorDef, ObservableDef) -- full-circuit `==` + a
hardcoded op-name sequence + assert_discriminates against a wrong-offset variant. The
QUBIT_COORDS `.get(q, [float(q)])` default is discriminated by a 3-qubit circuit whose metadata
supplies coords for qubits 0,1 but NOT 2 (2 -> default [2.0]); a no-metadata circuit exercises
the all-default arc. The rec-offset arithmetic (measurement_count += 1 -> the target_rec offsets)
is pinned by the exact DETECTOR/OBSERVABLE targets (a += mutant shifts the offsets -> `==` fails).
* _qubit_coords_from_metadata (via circuit_to_stim): the non-dict raise, the q<0 AND q>=num_qubits
raises (BOTH `or` operands, each exact -> kills `or`->`and`), and the empty-coords raise are each
tripped through a crafted CircuitIR.metadata with the EXACT message via assert_raises_exact.
* detector_error_model: pinned == circuit.detector_error_model(decompose_errors=True) for the
default AND == (...=False) when passed False, over a generated rotated surface-code circuit whose
True-vs-False DEMs DIFFER -> the default `decompose_errors=True` (and the arg threading) is killed
(a default->False mutant makes the default call return the False DEM != the True DEM).
* counts / StimCounts: pinned field-by-field vs INDEPENDENT reads straight off the stim.Circuit
(int(circuit.num_detectors)/num_observables/num_measurements/num_qubits) on a circuit whose four
counts are ALL DISTINCT (2,1,3,4) so any field<->property mis-mapping is caught; StimCounts is
asserted FROZEN (a frozen=True->False mutant is killed by the FrozenInstanceError expectation).
* write_stim_circuit / load_stim_circuit / write_detector_error_model: tmp_path write->load
ROUND-TRIP (loaded == original) + file text == str(circuit)/str(dem) + the returned value is the
Path (a str-path input returns a Path, killing a removed Path() coercion).
* sample_detector_records: SEEDED. A deterministic circuit (X_ERROR(1.0)) with 1 detector (fires,
True) + 1 observable (0, False) pins the exact det/obs values + shapes + bool dtype -> the
det=[:, :n_det] / obs=[:, n_det:n_det+n_obs] SPLIT is load-bearing (a swapped/offset slice flips
the pinned values). A noisy circuit sampled TWICE with the SAME seed is asserted identical (kills
a dropped seed=seed). Float shots (8.0) is accepted (int(shots) coercion).
REACHABILITY (the D13/D18/D19 default-arg / guard-route lesson -- PROBED through the PUBLIC entry
point circuit_to_stim, never asserted). Every reachable guard of _qubit_coords_from_metadata is
tripped through a real CircuitIR.metadata route with the EXACT message. The private _record_targets
carries TWO DEFENSIVE raises that are structurally UNREACHABLE via circuit_to_stim(valid CircuitIR):
(a) `record key ... was not measured before this declaration` -- CircuitIR.__post_init__ (via
_require_known_keys) already REJECTS any DetectorDef/ObservableDef referencing an unmeasured
key, so key is ALWAYS in key_to_measurement_index; and
(b) `record key ... is not in the past` (offset >= 0) -- a key's measurement index is ALWAYS
strictly < the current measurement_count (the measurement precedes the declaration and the
count was incremented past it), so offset is ALWAYS negative.
The `not in` / `-` / `<=`/`<` variants of these guards ARE killed by the happy path (they flip a
valid input into a spurious raise -> circuit_to_stim raises -> the op-by-op pin fails); only the
message-content mutants and the offset `>= 0`->`> 0`/`== 0` variants survive as EQUIVALENT (offset
structurally < 0). Likewise the circuit_to_stim `else: raise TypeError(unknown circuit step)` arm
(marked `# pragma: no cover`) is exhaustive over CircuitStep -- a CircuitIR cannot carry a step of
an unknown type (__post_init__ rejects it) -- so its message mutant is EQUIVALENT. SRC-CLEANUP NOTE
(NOT applied here): these are redundant defense-in-depth guards behind CircuitIR's construction
contract; a future cleanup could drop them. NO exemptions + NO out_of_scope: every SCORED unit is
CPU-pure and every branch of its OWN AST body is REACHABLE through a public entry point.
